title: Bottom derived unit through good lower truncation
statement: Let C,D be abelian categories with derived categories, and assume C has enough injectives and K-injective resolutions. Let F:C→D be additive and preserve finite limits, I an arbitrary integer-indexed cochain complex, and n∈ℤ. Put J=F(I), H=H^n on D(D), and let e:H^n(J)≅H(Q_h(PJ)) be the inverse homotopy and derived homology factor comparisons. Let U be the right-derived unit at PI and let q=RF(s_I p_I), where s_I:Q_h(PI)≅QI is the quotient factor isomorphism and p_I:QI→tauGE n QI is the truncation projection. There exists d:H^n(F(truncGE n I))≅H(RF(tauGE n QI)) such that e H(U) H(q)=H^n(F(I.πTruncGE n)) d. This is a derived-unit and localization compatibility, with no cycle map or homology quotient in its statement.

proof.text: The good truncation sequence gives Q(truncGE n I) as the canonical lower truncation of QI, with its projection commuting. Uniqueness of the truncation triangle supplies its isomorphism to tauGE n QI.

On K=truncGE n I, upper truncation at n and negative vanishing reduce invertibility of H^n of the derived unit to the complex H^n(K) placed in degree n. Shift to zero, apply the single-object comparison normalized on the injective-resolution augmentation, and use that F preserves the augmentation kernel. Transport via bounded-below/unbounded derived compatibility.

Define d by the homology factor isomorphisms at F(K), H^n of the unit at K, and H^n of RF of the canonical localization/truncation isomorphism. Naturality of the unit at P(I→K) and the homology factors, together with the commuting projection, proves the displayed factorization. All factors defining d are invertible; zero and negative cutoff cases need no exception.

theorem derived_lower_truncation_unit_bridge
    {C : Type u} {D : Type u'} [Category.{v} C] [Category.{v'} D]
    [Abelian C] [Abelian D] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C] [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} D]
    [EnoughInjectives C] [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions C]
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F]
    (I : CochainComplex C ℤ) (n : ℤ) :
    let J := (F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I
    let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor D n
    let e := ((HomotopyCategory.homologyFunctorFactors D (.up ℤ) n).app J).symm ≪≫
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactorsh D n).app
        ((HomotopyCategory.quotient D (.up ℤ)).obj J)).symm
    let U := F.rightDerivedFunctorUnit.app ((HomotopyCategory.quotient C (.up ℤ)).obj I)
    let q := F.rightDerivedFunctor.map
      ((DerivedCategory.quotientCompQhIso C).hom.app I ≫
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ n).app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I))
    ∃ d : ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj (I.truncGE n)).homology n ≅
        H.obj (F.rightDerivedFunctor.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE n).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I))),
      e.hom ≫ H.map U ≫ H.map q =
        HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
          ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map (I.πTruncGE n)) n ≫ d.hom
